title: Present Working Directory
brief: Run `pwd` to display your current directory position in the filesystem tree.
successMessage: `pwd` prints the absolute pathname of your current location.

title: Directory Listing
brief: Use `ls` to list the files and folders inside your current directory.
successMessage: `ls` displays entries in the current directory.

title: Reveal Hidden Dotfiles
brief: In Linux, filenames beginning with a dot (`.`) are hidden by default. Use `ls -la` to inspect your home directory and view hidden configuration files.
successMessage: The `-a` flag reveals hidden files like `.bashrc` and `.profile`.

title: Changing Directories
brief: Use `cd Documents` to move into the Documents directory.
successMessage: You changed your working directory into `/home/student/Documents`.

title: Climbing Up (..)
brief: The special symbol `..` represents the parent directory. From `Documents`, use `cd ..` to return to your home directory.
successMessage: `cd ..` moves one level up in the directory hierarchy.

title: Display File Content
brief: Print the contents of `Documents/notes.txt` to the screen using `cat`.
successMessage: `cat` reads files sequentially and prints them to stdout.

title: First Few Lines (head -n)
brief: `Documents/data.csv` is long. Show only its first 3 lines using `head`.
successMessage: `head -n N` restricts output to the first N lines of a file.

title: Last Few Lines (tail -n)
brief: Show only the last 2 lines of `Documents/data.csv` using `tail`.
successMessage: `tail -n N` displays the final N lines of a file.

title: Wildcard Globbing (*)
brief: The shell expands wildcard patterns before the command runs. List every `.js` file inside `projects/web` with a single `*` pattern instead of typing the filenames.
successMessage: The shell expanded `projects/web/*.js` into matching filenames before passing them to `ls`.

title: Multiple Wildcards
brief: List every `.txt` file in `Documents` with one wildcard pattern.
successMessage: Wildcard expansion makes working with groups of files effortless.

title: Search Patterns with grep
brief: Find every line that contains the word `active` in `Documents/data.csv`. Use `grep`.

hints.text: `grep` takes the pattern first, then the file to search.

successMessage: `grep` filters input line-by-line against a pattern.

title: Case-Insensitive Grep (-i)
brief: `logs/app_errors.log` spells errors three ways: ERROR, Error and error. Find all of them with one `grep` search that ignores letter case.

hints.text: One short flag makes `grep` ignore case.

successMessage: `-i` tells grep to ignore case differences.

title: Inverting Matches (-v)
brief: `logs/app_errors.log` is mostly INFO noise. Use `grep` to show every line EXCEPT the ones containing INFO.

hints.text: One flag inverts a `grep` match, so it prints the lines that do NOT match.

successMessage: `-v` inverts grep, showing only lines that do NOT match.

title: Line Counting (wc -l)
brief: Count how many records `Documents/server_access.log` holds. Use `wc`.

hints.text: `wc` counts lines, words and bytes. One flag limits it to lines.

successMessage: `wc -l` counts the number of newline characters in a file.

title: Sorting Data (sort)
brief: `Documents/data.csv` is comma separated. Sort it by the 4th field, salary, in numeric order. `sort` needs to know the separator, which field, and that the field is a number.

hints.text: Three flags: one sets the field separator, one picks the field number, one forces numeric order.

successMessage: `sort` can organize tabular text by specific fields using `-t` and `-k`.

title: Field Extraction (cut)
brief: `Documents/data.csv` is comma separated. Print only field 2 (name) and field 4 (salary). Use `cut`.

hints.text: One flag sets the delimiter, another picks the fields. Separate the field numbers with a comma.

successMessage: `cut` slices columns out of delimited files with ease.

title: The Pipeline (grep | wc -l)
brief: Count how many requests in `Documents/server_access.log` returned status 401. Do it in a single line: search the log, then feed the matching lines straight into a counter.

hints.text: The `|` operator sends one command's output into the next one. `grep` finds the lines, `wc -l` counts them.

successMessage: The `|` pipe connected stdout of `grep` directly to stdin of `wc -l`.

title: Output Redirection (>)
brief: Save every ERROR line from `logs/app_errors.log` into a new file at `/tmp/critical_errors.txt`. Nothing should print to the screen.

hints.text: `>` sends a command's output into a file instead of the screen.

successMessage: `>` redirects stdout into a file, creating or overwriting it.

title: Append Redirection (>>)
brief: Add the line `Audit log verified` to the END of `/tmp/audit_trail.log` without erasing what is already in it.

hints.text: `>` overwrites a file. A doubled version of the same operator appends instead. Use `echo` to produce the text.

successMessage: `>>` appends to a file without overwriting previous contents.

title: Split Output (tee)
brief: Show every line containing `Security` from `Documents/data.csv` on screen AND save those same lines to `/tmp/security_team.txt`, in one command.

hints.text: `tee` writes its input to a file and passes it along to the screen at the same time.

successMessage: `tee` duplicates its input stream, writing to both files and stdout.

title: Create Empty Files (touch)
brief: Create an empty file at `/tmp/new_file.txt`.

hints.text: `touch` creates an empty file, or updates the timestamp of one that exists.

successMessage: `touch` creates files if they do not exist or updates their timestamps.

title: Make Directories (mkdir -p)
brief: Create the directory `projects/api`. Use the flag that also creates any missing parent directory, so the command works whether or not `projects` already exists.

hints.text: `mkdir` makes directories. One flag creates missing parents and stays quiet if the directory is already there.

successMessage: `mkdir -p` creates nested parent directories automatically.

title: Copy Files (cp)
brief: Make a backup copy of `Documents/notes.txt` at `/tmp/notes_backup.txt`.

hints.text: `cp` takes the source path first, then the destination path.

successMessage: `cp` creates a duplicate of a file at the target path.

title: Recursive Copy (cp -r)
brief: Copy the whole `projects/web` directory, with everything inside it, to `/tmp/web_backup`.

hints.text: `cp` refuses a directory until you add the recursive flag.

successMessage: `-r` allows copying complete directory trees.

title: Move & Rename (mv)
brief: Rename `projects/scripts/deploy.py` to `deploy_prod.py`. Leave it in the same directory.

hints.text: `mv` both moves and renames. Give it the old path, then the new path.

successMessage: `mv` renames files or moves them to new directory locations.

title: Remove Files (rm)
brief: Delete the temporary file `/tmp/scratch.txt`.

hints.text: `rm` removes a file. There is no undo and no recycle bin.

successMessage: `rm` unlinks files from the filesystem.

title: Permissions (chmod octal)
brief: Lock down `Documents/notes.txt` so the owner can read and write it and nobody else can do anything at all. Set the octal mode.

hints.text: Read is 4, write is 2, execute is 1. Add them up per column: owner, group, other.

successMessage: Mode 600 (`-rw-------`) restricts access strictly to the owner.

title: Make Executable (chmod +x)
brief: `projects/scripts/deploy.py` cannot be run yet. Add execute permission to it.

hints.text: `chmod` also accepts symbolic modes: a `+` or `-`, then a letter for the permission.

successMessage: `+x` marks scripts and binaries as executable.

title: Inspect Inodes & Timestamps (stat)
brief: Show the size, permissions, inode number and timestamps of `Documents/notes.txt`. `ls -l` does not show all of that.

hints.text: One command reports a file's full metadata block.

successMessage: `stat` displays detailed inode metadata.

title: Superuser Elevation (sudo)
brief: `/etc/shadow` holds the account password hashes, and only root may read it, so `cat /etc/shadow` is denied. Read the file anyway.

hints.text: One command runs a single other command as a different user, normally root.

successMessage: `sudo` executes commands with effective UID 0 (root).
commandCheckExemptReason: Intentionally fails: the challenge teaches Permission denied and the sudo escalation that fixes it.

title: Finding Files by Name (find)
brief: Shell scripts are scattered somewhere under your home directory. List every file whose name ends in `.sh`, at any depth below the current directory.

hints.text: `find` walks a whole directory tree. It can filter on the filename, and the pattern should be quoted so the shell does not expand it first.

successMessage: `find` traverses directory trees searching by pattern.

title: Filtering by Type (find -type f)
brief: List every regular file underneath `projects` — the files themselves, not the directories that hold them.

hints.text: `find` can filter by entry type. The letter for a regular file is `f`.

successMessage: `-type f` restricts matches strictly to regular files, excluding directories.

title: Stream Editing (sed s///)
brief: Print `Documents/data.csv` with every occurrence of `Engineering` replaced by `Tech`. The file on disk must not change.

hints.text: `sed` edits a stream as it passes through. Its substitute script has the form s/old/new/g.

successMessage: `sed s/find/replace/g` transforms text streams with regex substitutions.

title: Pattern Scanning (awk)
brief: `/etc/passwd` is colon separated. Print only the username (field 1) and the home directory (field 6) for every account on the system.

hints.text: `awk` splits each line into numbered fields. One flag sets the separator, and `$1` refers to the first field.

successMessage: `awk` processes structured columns with powerful built-in field variables.

title: Variable Expansion & Quotes
brief: Print the value of your `HOME` variable. Quote it in the way that still lets the shell expand it.

hints.text: Double quotes allow variable expansion. Single quotes suppress it and print the name literally.

successMessage: "$HOME" expands to /home/student. If you typed '$HOME', the shell would print literal $HOME.

title: Exit Codes ($?)
brief: Every program returns an exit code: 0 means success, anything else means failure. Search `/etc/passwd` for `root`, then print the exit code that the search returned — both on one line.

hints.text: `$?` holds the exit code of the previous command, and `;` separates two commands on one line.

successMessage: $? holds the exit status of the previous command (0 = match found).

title: Conditional AND (&&)
brief: On one line, create the directory `/tmp/test_dir` and then create the file `/tmp/test_dir/file.txt` inside it — but only attempt the file if the directory step succeeded.

hints.text: `&&` runs the second command only when the first one exits with success.

successMessage: `cmd1 && cmd2` chains commands safely.

title: Conditional OR (||)
brief: On one line, try to read `/non_existent_file`, and if that attempt fails, print the message `File was missing`.

hints.text: `||` runs the second command only when the first one fails.

successMessage: `cmd1 || cmd2` provides reliable error recovery in shell scripts.

title: Compare Files (diff)
brief: Compare `projects/web/index.html` against `projects/web/style.css` line by line, in the unified format that patch tools read.

hints.text: `diff` compares two files. One flag selects unified output.

successMessage: `diff -u` outputs unified diffs showing line additions and removals.

title: Shell Mastery (history)
brief: Show every command you have typed in this session.

hints.text: The shell keeps a numbered list of what you have run. One word prints it.

successMessage: Congratulations! You have completed Linux Fundamentals and mastered core Unix shell engineering.
